appraisal_events.evidence: M. de Charlus était un peu fou ... on eût cru entendre crier un dément.
appraisal_events.explanation: Comparing Charlus's emphatic, theatrical manner of speech to an actor's or orator's affectation, the narrator concludes he is somewhat mad, an eccentricity society tacitly indulges rather than endorses.

appraisal_events.evidence: il niât me connaître ... c'est ce que je ne pouvais comprendre
appraisal_events.explanation: Despite having just professed eagerness to meet the narrator, Charlus denies knowing him to his own admiring sister-in-law, an inexplicable disavowal that the narrator flags as unaccountable.

status_effects.explanation: Charlus is cast as privately half-mad in his theatrical excess and then, minutes later, behaves in a manner the narrator finds bafflingly irrational by denying an acquaintance he had just claimed to want.
Charlus's denial of knowing him, made to the sister-in-law who esteems him highly, shuts the narrator out of the acknowledged acquaintance Charlus had just professed to want.

ambiguities: The narrator first offers a charitable explanation (Charlus misheard his name) but the closing lines suggest the denial is stranger than mere mishearing, given that Charlus knew the narrator through both his aunt and his nephew; the passage does not resolve which reading dominates.
